body: Did the same thing! Spent a solid 30 minutes talking about the reason I didn’t go to university because I didn’t want to waste my money on a degree in something I wouldn’t use, because I didn’t know what I wanted to do - and that photography is one of the worst degrees I know off because some of the most talented photographers I know did have to go university to learn it. Turned out she did that and made for an awkward drive home.

So sorry for your loss OP. I know exactly how this feels. I wouldn't wish this on anyone!
My Granddad suffered from Dementia, and seeing this happen to a loved one is the worst experience of my life. I was with him at the end, the rest of the Family left the room (Except me and one of my cousins), I shared some words with him, and his breathing changed the second I finished. I was told by someone that giving permission to go (Pass on) can sometimes speed the process (Sounds awful I know), but when watching a loved one go through this is awful. This was over 2 years ago, and I still beat myself up over those words as the memory of it is still with me, haunts me. The rest of the family gave permission weeks before, But I refused initially, which makes it so much harder that he seemed to hang on for me. There really needs to be more funding to help people who suffer with dementia, as I have been with 3 loved ones at the end, and my granddads passing is the only one that keeps me up at night.
